## Blog draft to pull request (drafts only)

**NOT imported into or tested on a running n8n instance.** Written from n8n documentation and source. Check every node on a real instance before turning it on.

What it does: runs weekly (or by hand), screens the topic against the public search index, asks a language model for a draft in the blogDraftSchema shape, runs cheap pre-checks, then creates a branch, writes `apps/web/content-drafts/<slug>.json` and opens a pull request titled "Draft: <title>". It then emails the reviewer.

What it never does: publish, merge, approve, edit existing content, contact anyone outside the organisation, or read participant data. The CI content gates and a named human reviewer decide what happens next (docs/21 sections 2 and 3).

Setup: see automation/n8n/README.md and credentials.md. Environment variables used: SITE_BASE_URL, BLOG_TOPIC_BRIEF, BLOG_AUTHOR_NAME, LLM_API_URL, LLM_MODEL, GITHUB_REPO_OWNER, GITHUB_REPO_NAME, GITHUB_BASE_BRANCH, NOTIFY_FROM_ADDRESS, EDITORIAL_NOTIFY_ADDRESS.

## Language model step

The prompt carries the rules from packages/schemas/src/blog.ts: quality gates, no participant data, a human author (added by the workflow, never by the model), at least 2 sources from the authoritative list, no banned wording.

The request body shape is a generic messages-style example. It must be adapted to the chosen provider, together with the response extraction in the Pre-checks node. Source URLs come from the model and are NOT fetched or verified here: the reviewer must open each one.
